home.faqSubtitle: Common questions about bank identifiers and the FinCode API.
home.faq1Q: Does a valid IBAN mean the bank account exists?
home.faq1A: No. IBAN validation confirms the format, length and MOD-97 checksum of the number. It cannot confirm that the account is open at the bank. Always treat validation as a format check, not an account existence check.
home.faq2Q: What is the difference between SWIFT and BIC?
home.faq2A: They refer to the same code. BIC (Bank Identifier Code) is defined by ISO 9362 and is often called a SWIFT code because it is managed by SWIFT. A BIC has 8 characters, or 11 when a branch code is appended.
home.faq3Q: What is a routing number checksum?
home.faq3A: US ABA routing numbers are 9 digits. The 9th digit is a checksum computed from the first 8 digits using the repeating weights 3, 7, 1. Our validator applies this algorithm before returning a result.
home.faq4Q: Where does the data come from?
home.faq4A: Every identifier record carries a data source: official registries such as the ISO 13616 IBAN registry, the ABA routing number registrar, Pay.UK, the RBI IFSC directory and published CNAPS participant lists. Retrieval dates and verification status are always shown.
home.faq5A: Yes. The Free plan includes 500 API requests per month at 10 requests per minute — enough to evaluate the full identifier coverage before upgrading.
home.faq6A: IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, US routing numbers, UK sort codes, Australian BSB, Indian IFSC and China CNAPS codes, plus bank, branch and country reference data. LEI, CHIPS and SEPA coverage is planned for V2.

swift.metaDescription: Search SWIFT/BIC codes (ISO 9362) for banks worldwide. Find bank name, country, city and branch from any SWIFT code.
swift.title: SWIFT/BIC Lookup
swift.subtitle: Look up any SWIFT/BIC code to find the bank, country and location behind it.
swift.whatBody: A SWIFT code — also called a BIC (Bank Identifier Code, ISO 9362) — identifies a bank branch in international payments. It is 8 characters long, or 11 when a branch code is included: 4 letters for the institution, 2 letters for the ISO country code, 2 characters for the location, and an optional 3-character branch code.
swift.formatBody: BBBB CC LL bbb — institution (4 letters), country (2 letters), location (2 alphanumeric), branch (3 alphanumeric, optional). 'XXX' in the branch position means head office.
swift.count: {count, plural, =0 {No SWIFT codes} one {# SWIFT code} other {# SWIFT codes}}
swift.metaDescriptionDetail: SWIFT/BIC code {code} belongs to {bank} ({country}). See structure, location, related identifiers and data source.
swift.detailFaq1Q: Is a SWIFT code the same as a BIC?
swift.detailFaq1A: Yes — BIC (Bank Identifier Code) is the ISO 9362 standard name and SWIFT code is the common name. Both refer to the 8 or 11 character bank identifier.
swift.detailFaq2Q: What does 'XXX' at the end of a SWIFT code mean?
swift.detailFaq2A: It identifies the bank's head office rather than a specific branch. An 8-character code without a branch code also refers to the head office.

routing.metaDescription: Look up US ABA routing numbers with checksum validation. Find the bank, city and state behind any 9-digit routing number.
routing.title: Routing Number Lookup
routing.subtitle: Look up US ABA routing numbers with checksum validation.
routing.whatBody: An ABA routing number (Routing Transit Number) is a 9-digit code that identifies a US financial institution. The first 4 digits identify the Federal Reserve district and institution; the next 4 identify the bank itself; the 9th digit is a checksum computed with the weights 3, 7, 1.
routing.count: {count, plural, =0 {No routing numbers} one {# routing number} other {# routing numbers}}
routing.metaDescriptionDetail: ABA routing number {code} belongs to {bank} ({country}). Checksum-validated, with bank details and related identifiers.
routing.detailFaq1Q: Can a routing number be validated offline?
routing.detailFaq1A: Yes — the 9th digit is a checksum over the first 8 digits using the repeating weights 3, 7, 1. The checksum catches most transcription errors.
routing.detailFaq2Q: Do routing numbers differ for wires and ACH?
routing.detailFaq2A: Yes — many US banks publish separate routing numbers for Fedwire and ACH. Always confirm which rail your payment requires.

sortCode.metaDescription: Look up UK bank sort codes (6 digits, formatted xx-xx-xx) and find the bank behind each code.
sortCode.title: Sort Code Lookup
sortCode.subtitle: Look up UK bank sort codes and the institutions behind them.
sortCode.whatBody: A sort code is a 6-digit number that identifies a bank and branch in the UK and Ireland. It is usually written as three pairs, e.g. 20-00-00. Together with the account number it routes domestic payments.
sortCode.count: {count, plural, =0 {No sort codes} one {# sort code} other {# sort codes}}
sortCode.metaDescriptionDetail: UK sort code {code} belongs to {bank}. See the institution, related identifiers and data source.
sortCode.detailFaq1Q: Is a sort code unique to one branch?
sortCode.detailFaq1A: Sort codes are allocated per institution and branch. Some banks also use universal codes that apply bank-wide.
sortCode.detailFaq2Q: Do I need an IBAN for UK payments?
sortCode.detailFaq2A: Domestic UK payments use sort code plus account number. For cross-border payments an IBAN is recommended — the UK IBAN embeds the sort code.

bsb.metaDescription: Look up Australian BSB (Bank State Branch) numbers and find the bank behind each code.
bsb.title: BSB Lookup
bsb.subtitle: Look up Australian Bank State Branch numbers.
bsb.whatBody: A BSB (Bank State Branch) is a 6-digit code that identifies an Australian bank branch, written as xxx-xxx. The first 2-3 digits identify the bank; the remaining digits identify the branch.
bsb.count: {count, plural, =0 {No BSB codes} one {# BSB code} other {# BSB codes}}
bsb.metaDescriptionDetail: Australian BSB {code} belongs to {bank}. See the institution, related identifiers and data source.
bsb.detailFaq1Q: Is a BSB unique to a branch?
bsb.detailFaq1A: A BSB identifies a bank branch, or a bank-wide universal BSB. The account number is still required for routing.
bsb.detailFaq2Q: Do I need an IBAN for Australia?
bsb.detailFaq2A: Australia does not participate in IBAN — payments use BSB plus account number, plus the beneficiary bank's SWIFT/BIC for inbound international transfers.

ifsc.metaDescription: Look up Indian Financial System Codes (IFSC) and find the bank and branch behind each code.
ifsc.title: IFSC Lookup
ifsc.subtitle: Look up Indian Financial System Codes (IFSC).
ifsc.whatBody: An IFSC (Indian Financial System Code) is an 11-character code assigned by the Reserve Bank of India: 4 letters identifying the bank, a literal 0, and 6 characters identifying the branch. It is required for NEFT, RTGS and IMPS transfers.
ifsc.count: {count, plural, =0 {No IFSC codes} one {# IFSC code} other {# IFSC codes}}
ifsc.metaDescriptionDetail: Indian IFSC {code} belongs to {bank}. See the bank, branch information and data source.
ifsc.detailFaq1Q: What does the fifth character of an IFSC mean?
ifsc.detailFaq1A: It is always zero — a reserved character in the RBI IFSC standard, which makes the format easy to recognize.
ifsc.detailFaq2Q: Where is the official IFSC list published?
ifsc.detailFaq2A: The Reserve Bank of India publishes the master directory of IFSC codes. FinCode only shows RBI-sourced records with retrieval dates.

cnaps.metaDescription: Look up China CNAPS codes (12-digit bank identification numbers) and find the bank and branch behind each code.
cnaps.title: CNAPS Lookup
cnaps.subtitle: Look up China National Advanced Payment System codes.
cnaps.whatBody: A CNAPS code is a 12-digit number that identifies a bank branch in China's payment system (also called the bank identification number or 联行号). The first 3 digits identify the bank, the next 8 the city and branch, and the last digit is a check digit.
cnaps.count: {count, plural, =0 {No CNAPS codes} one {# CNAPS code} other {# CNAPS codes}}
cnaps.metaDescriptionDetail: CNAPS code {code} belongs to {bank} ({country}). See branch information, bank code and related identifiers.
cnaps.detailFaq1Q: Is a CNAPS code the same as a bank code?
cnaps.detailFaq1A: No — the 3-digit bank code identifies the bank, while the full 12-digit CNAPS code identifies a specific branch in the payment system.
cnaps.detailFaq2Q: Where do CNAPS codes come from?
cnaps.detailFaq2A: They are assigned within China's National Advanced Payment System operated by the People's Bank of China, and published in participant lists.

about.metaDescription: FinCode is a global financial data platform: bank identifiers, account formats and financial institution data through one API.
about.title: About FinCode
about.subtitle: Global bank identifier data, done properly.
about.missionBody: Cross-border payments fail every day because bank identifiers are entered by hand from a dozen different national registries. FinCode brings IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, routing numbers, sort codes, BSB, IFSC and CNAPS data into one validated, source-attributed API so developers never have to scrape a registry again.
about.principle1: Data first — every record is sourced, versioned and auditable.
about.principle2: API first — one consistent contract across every identifier type.
about.principle3: Honest validation — format checks never pretend to prove account existence.
about.principle4: Backwards compatibility — APIs evolve without breaking integrations.
about.sourcesBody: Identifier records are compiled from official registries and published directories. The source, license and retrieval date of every dataset is shown alongside the data.

legal.privacyMetaDescription: FinCode privacy policy: what data we collect, how API usage is measured, and how information is protected.
legal.termsMetaDescription: FinCode terms of service for the website and the Global Financial Data API.
legal.preview: This preview policy will be finalized with the production launch (FIN-032).
legal.privacyIntro: FinCode is built for developers, and this policy explains in plain language what we collect and why.
legal.privacyCollectionBody: Account information (email, organization), API usage metrics (endpoint, status code, response time — never full IBANs or account numbers), and standard website analytics. Sensitive payment identifiers are masked in logs and are never sold or shared.
legal.privacyUsageBody: Usage records store the API key ID, endpoint, status code and latency. We do not store the full financial identifiers submitted to validation endpoints beyond short-lived caches.
legal.privacyContactBody: For privacy questions, contact the team via the contact page.
legal.termsIntro: These terms govern the use of the FinCode website and API.
legal.termsDataBody: Identifier data is compiled from official and public sources with the retrieval date shown on each record. It is provided for reference and validation purposes; users remain responsible for confirming critical payment details with their bank.
legal.termsAccountsBody: API keys are confidential. Store only the key hash, rotate keys regularly, and revoke keys that may have been exposed.
legal.termsChangesBody: We may update these terms; continued use after changes are published constitutes acceptance.
